title: Chart Types
text: myIO supports 20 chart types via type argument addIoLayer(). vignette shows example . examples use built-R datasets can copy run directly.

title: Chart Types
text: Chart types organized compatibility groups. can freely combine types within compatible groups (e.g. point + line + area), standalone types like treemap gauge mixed types. Continuous, categorical, binned groups can combined . Matrix standalone groups mixed groups.

title: Chart Types
code: myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "line",     color = "steelblue",     label = "temperature",     data = airquality,     mapping = list(x_var = "Day", y_var = "Temp")   )

title: Chart Types
code: myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "point",     color = "coral",     label = "scatter",     data = mtcars,     mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")   )

title: Chart Types
code: myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "bar",     color = "steelblue",     label = "bars",     data = mtcars,     mapping = list(x_var = "cyl", y_var = "mpg")   ) |>   defineCategoricalAxis(xAxis = TRUE)

title: Chart Types
text: Area charts require x_var, low_y, high_y mapping:
code: aq <- airquality[complete.cases(airquality), ] aq$TempLow <- aq$Temp - 5 aq$TempHigh <- aq$Temp + 5  myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "area",     color = "lightsteelblue",     label = "area",     data = aq,     mapping = list(x_var = "Day", low_y = "TempLow", high_y = "TempHigh")   )

title: Chart Types
code: myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "groupedBar",     color = "steelblue",     label = "grouped",     data = mtcars,     mapping = list(x_var = "cyl", y_var = "mpg")   ) |>   defineCategoricalAxis(xAxis = TRUE)

title: Chart Types
text: Histograms use value mapping instead x_var/y_var:
code: myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "histogram",     color = "steelblue",     label = "hist",     data = mtcars,     mapping = list(value = "mpg")   )

title: Chart Types
code: myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "donut",     color = c("#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73"),     label = "donut",     data = aggregate(mpg ~ cyl, data = mtcars, FUN = mean),     mapping = list(x_var = "cyl", y_var = "mpg")   )

title: Chart Types
text: Gauges use value mapping:
code: myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "gauge",     color = "steelblue",     label = "gauge",     data = data.frame(value = 0.75),     mapping = list(value = "value")   )

title: Chart Types
code: myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "hexbin",     color = "steelblue",     label = "hexbin",     data = mtcars,     mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg", radius = 20)   )

title: Chart Types
text: Treemaps use different mapping level_1 level_2 instead x_var y_var:
code: myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "treemap",     label = "cars",     data = mtcars,     mapping = list(level_1 = "vs", level_2 = "cyl")   )

title: Chart Types
text: Heatmaps display matrix values continuous color scale. axes categorical. Mapping requires x_var, y_var, value:
code: df <- expand.grid(   quarter = c("Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"),   segment = c("Low", "Mid", "High"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) df$value <- c(2, 4, 6, 5, 7, 9, 4, 6, 8, 3, 5, 7)  myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "heatmap",     color = "#4E79A7",     label = "Revenue",     data = df,     mapping = list(x_var = "quarter", y_var = "segment", value = "value")   ) |>   defineCategoricalAxis(xAxis = TRUE, yAxis = TRUE) |>   setAxisFormat(xLabel = "Quarter", yLabel = "Segment")

title: Chart Types
text: Calendar heatmaps render daily values GitHub-contributions-style grid: one cell per day, seven rows per week, month labels across top. chart scoped single calendar year v1.2. Mapping requires date (Date ISO "YYYY-MM-DD" string) value (numeric): Use options$weekStart = "monday" ISO week ordering. Two calendars linked via linkCharts(, b, = "day", cursor = TRUE) synchronize hover crosshair date across charts.
code: set.seed(42) df <- data.frame(   day     = as.Date("2026-01-01") + 0:364,   commits = rpois(365, lambda = 3) )  myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "calendarHeatmap",     color = "#4E79A7",     label = "Daily commits",     data = df,     mapping = list(date = "day", value = "commits")   )

title: Chart Types
text: Candlestick charts show open-high-low-close data. Green bars indicate close >= open, red bars indicate close < open. Mapping requires x_var, open, high, low, close:
code: df <- data.frame(   day = 1:10,   open  = c(10, 12, 11, 14, 13, 15, 14, 16, 15, 17),   high  = c(14, 15, 14, 17, 16, 18, 17, 19, 18, 20),   low   = c(9,  11, 10, 13, 12, 14, 13, 15, 14, 16),   close = c(12, 11, 14, 13, 15, 14, 16, 15, 17, 19) )  myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "candlestick",     label = "Price",     data = df,     mapping = list(       x_var = "day", open = "open",       high = "high", low = "low", close = "close"     )   ) |>   setAxisFormat(xAxis = ".0f", yAxis = "$,.0f",                 xLabel = "Day", yLabel = "Price")

title: Chart Types
text: Waterfall charts show initial value affected sequential positive negative changes. cumulative transform auto-applied. Mark summary rows total mapping:
code: df <- data.frame(   step  = c("Revenue", "COGS", "Gross Profit", "OpEx", "Net Income"),   value = c(500, -200, NA, -150, NA),   is_total = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE) )  myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "waterfall",     label = "P&L",     data = df,     mapping = list(x_var = "step", y_var = "value", total = "is_total")   ) |>   defineCategoricalAxis(xAxis = TRUE) |>   setAxisFormat(yAxis = "$,.0f", xLabel = "Step", yLabel = "Amount")

title: Chart Types
text: Sankey diagrams show flows nodes. Mapping requires source, target, value. standalone type mixed charts:
code: df <- data.frame(   source = c("Budget", "Budget", "Sales", "Sales", "Marketing"),   target = c("Sales", "Marketing", "Revenue", "Leads", "Leads"),   value  = c(40, 20, 30, 10, 15) )  myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "sankey",     color = c("#4E79A7", "#F28E2B", "#E15759", "#76B7B2", "#59A14F"),     label = "Flow",     data = df,     mapping = list(source = "source", target = "target", value = "value")   )

title: Chart Types
text: Boxplots composite charts automatically expand area (IQR box), point (whiskers, median), optional outlier layers. Mapping requires x_var (categorical) y_var (numeric): Options: showOutliers (default TRUE), whiskerType (“tukey” “minmax”).
code: myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "boxplot",     color = "#4E79A7",     label = "Sepal Length",     data = iris,     mapping = list(x_var = "Species", y_var = "Sepal.Length"),     options = list(showOutliers = TRUE)   ) |>   setAxisFormat(xLabel = "Species", yLabel = "Sepal Length (cm)")

title: Chart Types
text: Violin plots show distribution shape via mirrored kernel density estimate. expand area (density), optional box (IQR), optional median point layers: Options: showBox (TRUE), showMedian (TRUE), showPoints (FALSE), bandwidth (KDE bandwidth, default “nrd0”).
code: myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "violin",     color = "#59A14F",     label = "Distribution",     data = iris,     mapping = list(x_var = "Species", y_var = "Sepal.Length"),     options = list(showBox = TRUE, showMedian = TRUE)   ) |>   setAxisFormat(xLabel = "Species", yLabel = "Sepal Length (cm)")

title: Chart Types
text: Ridgeline plots stack multiple density curves vertically comparing distributions across groups. expand one area sub-layer per group value. Mapping requires x_var (numeric values), y_var (numeric), group (categorical): Options: overlap (0-1, default 0.6), bandwidth (KDE bandwidth).
code: df <- mtcars df$cyl <- as.character(df$cyl)  myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "ridgeline",     color = c("#4E79A7", "#F28E2B", "#E15759"),     label = "MPG by Cylinders",     data = df,     mapping = list(x_var = "hp", y_var = "mpg", group = "cyl"),     options = list(overlap = 0.5)   ) |>   setAxisFormat(xLabel = "Horsepower", yLabel = "Cylinders")

title: Chart Types
text: Q-Q (quantile-quantile) plots compare sample quantiles theoretical distribution assess normality. composite expands point layer (Q-Q scatter), reference line (Q1/Q3), optional confidence envelope. y_var required mapping: Options: envelope (TRUE), conf_level (0.95), distribution (“norm”), qfunc (custom quantile function). Supports grouped Q-Q via group mapping.
code: myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "qq",     color = "#4E79A7",     label = "MPG Normality",     data = mtcars,     mapping = list(y_var = "mpg")   ) |>   setAxisFormat(xLabel = "Theoretical Quantiles", yLabel = "Sample Quantiles")

title: Chart Types
text: Comparison plots combine boxplots pairwise significance brackets showing p-values hypothesis tests. composite expands boxplot sub-layers plus bracket layer test results: Options: method (“t.test” “wilcox.test”), p_adjust (“none”, “bonferroni”, “holm”, “BH”), comparisons (list specific pairs), showOutliers (TRUE).
code: myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "comparison",     color = "#4E79A7",     label = "Species Comparison",     data = iris,     mapping = list(x_var = "Species", y_var = "Sepal.Width"),     options = list(method = "t.test", p_adjust = "bonferroni")   ) |>   setAxisFormat(xLabel = "Species", yLabel = "Sepal Width (cm)")

title: Chart Types
text: Brackets can also added standalone layer top grouped chart. Use transform = "pairwise_test" compute significance tests:
code: myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "boxplot", color = "#4E79A7",     label = "Sepal Width", data = iris,     mapping = list(x_var = "Species", y_var = "Sepal.Width")   ) |>   addIoLayer(     type = "bracket", label = "Tests",     transform = "pairwise_test", data = iris,     mapping = list(x_var = "Species", y_var = "Sepal.Width"),     options = list(method = "wilcox.test", p_adjust = "holm")   )

title: Chart Types
text: can overlay compatible chart types single widget. layer points, connecting line, linear model trend line:
code: myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "point",     color = "steelblue",     label = "points",     data = mtcars,     mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")   ) |>   addIoLayer(     type = "line",     color = "orange",     label = "line",     data = mtcars,     mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")   ) |>   addIoLayer(     type = "line",     transform = "lm",     color = "red",     label = "trend",     data = mtcars,     mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")   )

title: Linking myIO with Crosstalk
text: v1.2, nine chart-layer types respond crosstalk selection filter events: Aggregate layer types (boxplot, violin, qq, regression, density, ridgeline, survfit, comparison) participate v1.2. drive selection aggregate views, layer linked scatter next aggregate chart.

title: Linking myIO with Crosstalk
text: Selection dims non-matching elements (sets CSS opacity --chart-brush-dim-opacity variable). widgets affected layout. Filter hides non-matching elements entirely (display: none). Use linked partners filter UI — e.g. crosstalk::filter_select() dropdown — genuinely narrows dataset. Pass filter = TRUE setLinked() enable filter-driven hiding.

title: Linking myIO with Crosstalk
text: setLinked(mode = ...) accepts three values: "source" — chart emits selections (via brush) react incoming ones. "target" — chart reacts incoming selections emit . "" (default) — bidirectional.

title: Linking myIO with Crosstalk
text: Brush rectangle chart: matching rows table stay bold rest dim. Click rows table: matching points stay solid, rest dim.
code: library(crosstalk) library(myIO) library(DT)  shared <- SharedData$new(mtcars, key = ~rownames(mtcars))  bscols(   widths = c(7, 5),   myIO(data = shared$data()) |>     addIoLayer(       type = "point", label = "cars",       mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")     ) |>     setBrush(direction = "xy") |>     setLinked(shared),   datatable(shared, rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 5)) )

title: Linking myIO with Crosstalk
code: library(crosstalk) library(myIO) library(reactable)  # Aggregate mtcars by cyl for a simple lollipop by_cyl <- data.frame(   cyl = c("4", "6", "8"),   avg_mpg = c(     mean(mtcars$mpg[mtcars$cyl == 4]),     mean(mtcars$mpg[mtcars$cyl == 6]),     mean(mtcars$mpg[mtcars$cyl == 8])   ) ) shared <- SharedData$new(by_cyl, key = ~cyl)  bscols(   widths = c(6, 6),   myIO(data = shared$data()) |>     addIoLayer(       type = "lollipop", label = "by-cyl",       mapping = list(x_var = "cyl", y_var = "avg_mpg")     ) |>     setLinked(shared),   reactable(shared, selection = "multiple", onClick = "select") )

title: Linking myIO with Crosstalk
text: plotly’s crosstalk integration means can link myIO chart directly plotly chart SharedData: evaluated vignette. Install plotly run locally.
code: library(crosstalk) library(myIO) library(plotly)  shared <- SharedData$new(mtcars, key = ~rownames(mtcars)) bscols(   myIO(data = shared$data()) |>     addIoLayer(type = "point", label = "m",                mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")) |>     setBrush(direction = "xy") |>     setLinked(shared),   plot_ly(shared, x = ~hp, y = ~mpg, type = "scatter", mode = "markers") )

title: Linking myIO with Crosstalk
text: evaluated vignette. Install leaflet run locally.
code: library(crosstalk) library(myIO) library(leaflet)  quakes_small <- head(quakes, 50) shared <- SharedData$new(quakes_small) bscols(   leaflet(shared) |> addTiles() |> addMarkers(),   myIO(data = shared$data()) |>     addIoLayer(type = "point", label = "mag",                mapping = list(x_var = "depth", y_var = "mag")) |>     setLinked(shared) )

title: LLM Tool Calling
text: Ask AI assistant “make box plot Sepal.Width Species myIO” confidently write something. Often subtly wrong: chart type doesn’t exist (scatterplot instead point), mapping key invented (value_var instead y_var), function argument wrong name (setAxisFormat(axis_x = ...)). code looks plausible fails runtime — worse, runs renders nothing. myIO ships pieces let AI check work commits: machine-readable description every chart can draw, validator flags structural mistakes suggests fix. result assistant can generate myIO chart, discover got name wrong, correct , hand working code.

title: LLM Tool Calling
text: short orientation; skip can rely familiar. Modern LLMs can given tools — functions describe model may call mid-conversation. Instead answering one shot, model can call tool, read result, revise. Tool calling loop. MCP (Model Context Protocol) standard way expose tools assistants like Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, configure MCP-aware client can use . myIO exposes six tools. two work validate_spec (chart description valid?) validate_call (function call valid?); four let model discover ’s available. ’re usable two ways: plain R functions (shown throughout article, every example real output) MCP server (covered end) assistants.

code: myio_list_chart_types() #>  [1] "line"            "point"           "bar"             "hexbin"          #>  [5] "treemap"         "gauge"           "donut"           "area"            #>  [9] "groupedBar"      "histogram"       "heatmap"         "candlestick"     #> [13] "waterfall"       "sankey"          "boxplot"         "violin"          #> [17] "ridgeline"       "rangeBar"        "text"            "regression"      #> [21] "bracket"         "comparison"      "qq"              "lollipop"        #> [25] "dumbbell"        "waffle"          "beeswarm"        "bump"            #> [29] "radar"           "funnel"          "parallel"        "survfit"         #> [33] "histogram_fit"   "calendarHeatmap" "quantile_dots"   "fan" attempt <- list(   type = "boxplot",   mapping = list(column_var = "Species", value_var = "Sepal.Width") ) as_json(myio_validate_spec(attempt)) #> { #>   "valid": false, #>   "errors": [ #>     { #>       "code": "MISSING_MAPPING", #>       "field": "x_var", #>       "message": "Missing required mapping 'x_var' for chart type 'boxplot'." #>     }, #>     { #>       "code": "MISSING_MAPPING", #>       "field": "y_var", #>       "message": "Missing required mapping 'y_var' for chart type 'boxplot'." #>     }, #>     { #>       "code": "UNKNOWN_MAPPING_KEY", #>       "field": "column_var", #>       "message": "Unknown mapping key 'column_var' for chart type 'boxplot'.", #>       "suggestion": "x_var" #>     }, #>     { #>       "code": "UNKNOWN_MAPPING_KEY", #>       "field": "value_var", #>       "message": "Unknown mapping key 'value_var' for chart type 'boxplot'.", #>       "suggestion": "y_var" #>     } #>   ] #> } fixed <- list(   type = "boxplot",   mapping = list(x_var = "Species", y_var = "Sepal.Width") ) as_json(myio_validate_spec(fixed)) #> { #>   "valid": true, #>   "errors": [] #> }

title: LLM Tool Calling
text: Putting together — pattern agent follows whether calls R functions MCP tools: Propose chart spec. Call validate_spec. valid false, apply suggestion error go 2. valid, validate accompanying set*() call validate_call. loop, run actual validator, converges broken attempt working spec without hard-coded knowledge myIO’s API:
code: spec <- list(type = "boxplot",              mapping = list(column_var = "Species", value_var = "Sepal.Width")) res  <- myio_validate_spec(spec)  while (!res$valid) {   for (err in res$errors) {     if (identical(err$code, "UNKNOWN_MAPPING_KEY") && !is.null(err$suggestion)) {       spec$mapping[[err$suggestion]] <- spec$mapping[[err$field]]       spec$mapping[[err$field]] <- NULL     }   }   res <- myio_validate_spec(spec) } as_json(spec) #> { #>   "type": "boxplot", #>   "mapping": { #>     "x_var": "Species", #>     "y_var": "Sepal.Width" #>   } #> }

title: Migrating from plotly to myIO
text: Three things changed 2025 make plotly risky dependency new work: Documentation retired. official plotly-r docs site went offline. Learning API now means reading source code archived pages. Broken statistical features. Regression CI bands (#1472) statistical annotations (#1687) broken years fix sight. Heavy dependency chain. plotly pulls htmlwidgets, tidyr, dplyr, rlang, full plotly.js bundle (~3.5 MB minified). myIO depends htmlwidgets jsonlite. charts need statistical overlays, cost working around plotly’s gaps exceeds cost switching.

title: Migrating from plotly to myIO
text: myIO uses layered pipe API instead single function mode flags.
code: # plotly plot_ly(mtcars, x = ~wt, y = ~mpg, type = "scatter", mode = "markers") # myIO myIO(data = mtcars) |>   addIoLayer(type = "point", label = "Cars",     mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg"))

title: Migrating from plotly to myIO
text: Groups declared mapping, top-level aesthetic.
code: # plotly plot_ly(economics_long, x = ~date, y = ~value, color = ~variable,         type = "scatter", mode = "lines") # myIO myIO(data = economics_long) |>   addIoLayer(type = "line", label = "Trends",     mapping = list(x_var = "date", y_var = "value", group = "variable"))

title: Migrating from plotly to myIO
text: myIO requires explicit defineCategoricalAxis() call discrete x-axes.
code: # plotly plot_ly(data.frame(x = c("A","B","C"), y = c(10,20,15)),         x = ~x, y = ~y, type = "bar") # myIO myIO(data = data.frame(x = c("A","B","C"), y = c(10,20,15))) |>   addIoLayer(type = "bar", label = "Values",     mapping = list(x_var = "x", y_var = "y")) |>   defineCategoricalAxis(xAxis = TRUE)

title: Migrating from plotly to myIO
text: Bin count set via options$bins rather layout parameter.
code: # plotly plot_ly(mtcars, x = ~mpg, type = "histogram") # myIO myIO(data = mtcars) |>   addIoLayer(type = "histogram", label = "MPG Distribution",     mapping = list(x_var = "mpg"),     options = list(bins = 15))

title: Migrating from plotly to myIO
text: myIO boxplots decompose sub-layers (IQR box, whiskers, median, outliers), independently styled interactive.
code: # plotly plot_ly(iris, y = ~Sepal.Length, color = ~Species, type = "box") # myIO myIO(data = iris) |>   addIoLayer(type = "boxplot", label = "Sepal Length",     mapping = list(x_var = "Species", y_var = "Sepal.Length"),     options = list(showOutliers = TRUE)) |>   defineCategoricalAxis(xAxis = TRUE)

title: Migrating from plotly to myIO
text: plotly #1472 – CI ribbons regression lines render correctly. myIO computes CI via stats::predict() renders first-class area layer – manual pre-computation.
code: # plotly (broken — CI band misaligns or disappears) model <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars) preds <- data.frame(wt = seq(min(mtcars$wt), max(mtcars$wt), length.out = 50)) preds <- cbind(preds, predict(model, preds, interval = "confidence")) plot_ly() |>   add_markers(data = mtcars, x = ~wt, y = ~mpg) |>   add_ribbons(data = preds, x = ~wt, ymin = ~lwr, ymax = ~upr) |>   add_lines(data = preds, x = ~wt, y = ~fit) # myIO (one call, CI computed internally) myIO(data = mtcars) |>   addIoLayer(type = "regression", label = "MPG vs Weight",     mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg"),     options = list(method = "lm", showCI = TRUE, showStats = TRUE))

title: Migrating from plotly to myIO
text: plotly #1687 – ggplotly() drops stat_compare_means() annotations. comparison composite expands boxplots plus significance brackets p-values, computed R rendered D3.js.
code: # plotly (annotations lost in ggplotly conversion) library(ggpubr) p <- ggboxplot(iris, x = "Species", y = "Sepal.Length") +   stat_compare_means(method = "t.test", comparisons = list(     c("setosa", "versicolor"), c("versicolor", "virginica"))) ggplotly(p)  # brackets and p-values vanish # myIO (pairwise tests rendered natively) myIO(data = iris) |>   addIoLayer(type = "comparison", label = "Sepal Length",     mapping = list(x_var = "Species", y_var = "Sepal.Length"),     options = list(method = "t.test"))

title: Migrating from plotly to myIO
text: myIO theming uses CSS custom properties, colors apply consistently across layers including CI bands, annotations, export buttons.
code: # plotly plot_ly(mtcars, x = ~wt, y = ~mpg, type = "scatter", mode = "markers") |>   layout(template = "plotly_dark") # myIO myIO(data = mtcars) |>   addIoLayer(type = "point", label = "Cars",     mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")) |>   setTheme(background = "#1a1a2e", text = "#e0e0e0",            grid = "#2a2a4a", font = "Inter")

text: multi-layer chart, pass named list keyed existing layer labels. stored keyframe complete snapshot. frame omits layer, layer retains data preceding frame. Target layer Latest actuals carries forward Quarter opening. Unknown layer names, unnamed lists, non-data-frame values, duplicate frame labels fail R widget serialized.
code: actual_1 <- data.frame(month = 1:3, value = c(10, 13, 17)) actual_2 <- data.frame(month = 1:4, value = c(10, 13, 17, 22)) target_1 <- data.frame(month = 1:3, value = c(12, 15, 18)) target_2 <- data.frame(month = 1:4, value = c(12, 15, 18, 21))  myIO() |>   addIoLayer(     type = "line", label = "Actual", data = actual_1,     mapping = list(x_var = "month", y_var = "value")   ) |>   addIoLayer(     type = "line", label = "Target", data = target_1,     mapping = list(x_var = "month", y_var = "value")   ) |>   addKeyframe(     list(Actual = actual_1, Target = target_1),     "Quarter opening"   ) |>   addKeyframe(     list(Actual = actual_2),     "Latest actuals"   ) |>   addKeyframe(     list(Actual = actual_2, Target = target_2),     "Revised target"   )

title: Sequential Storytelling with Keyframes
text: Keyframe inputs source data. myIO applies layer’s configured R transform storing snapshot, exactly layer created.
code: observed <- data.frame(x = 1:20, y = (1:20) + sin(1:20)) projected <- data.frame(x = 1:20, y = (1:20) * 1.4 + cos(1:20))  myIO(observed) |>   addIoLayer(     type = "line", label = "Trend", transform = "lm",     mapping = list(x_var = "x", y_var = "y")   ) |>   addKeyframe(observed, "Observed trend") |>   addKeyframe(projected, "Projected trend")

title: Sequential Storytelling with Keyframes

code: ui <- shiny::fluidPage(   myIOOutput("story"),   shiny::actionButton("next_frame", "Next"),   shiny::actionButton("show_baseline", "Baseline") )  server <- function(input, output, session) {   output$story <- renderMyIO({     myIO(start) |>       addIoLayer("line", label = "Revenue",         mapping = list(x_var = "year", y_var = "value")) |>       addKeyframe(start, "Baseline") |>       addKeyframe(growth, "Growth case") |>       addKeyframe(outlook, "Outlook")   })    shiny::observeEvent(input$next_frame, {     myIOProxy("story", session) |> stepKeyframe("next")   })   shiny::observeEvent(input$show_baseline, {     myIOProxy("story", session) |> setKeyframe("Baseline")   }) }  shiny::shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Shiny Integration
text: myIO provides standard htmlwidgets Shiny bindings, charts work like output Shiny app. vignette covers basics, interactive /O patterns, common recipes.

title: Shiny Integration
text: Use myIOOutput() UI renderMyIO() server:
code: library(shiny) library(myIO)  ui <- fluidPage(   titlePanel("myIO + Shiny"),   myIOOutput("chart", width = "100%", height = "400px") )  server <- function(input, output) {   output$chart <- renderMyIO({     myIO() |>       addIoLayer(         type = "point",         color = "steelblue",         label = "scatter",         data = mtcars,         mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")       )   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Shiny Integration
text: renderMyIO() reactive, chart updates automatically inputs change. Use standard Shiny reactivity filter transform data:
code: library(shiny) library(myIO)  ui <- fluidPage(   titlePanel("Reactive myIO Chart"),   sidebarLayout(     sidebarPanel(       selectInput("cyl", "Cylinders:",         choices = c("All", sort(unique(mtcars$cyl))),         selected = "All"       ),       selectInput("chart_type", "Chart Type:",         choices = c("point", "bar", "line"),         selected = "point"       )     ),     mainPanel(       myIOOutput("chart", height = "500px")     )   ) )  server <- function(input, output) {   filtered_data <- reactive({     if (input$cyl == "All") mtcars else mtcars[mtcars$cyl == as.numeric(input$cyl), ]   })    output$chart <- renderMyIO({     myIO() |>       addIoLayer(         type = input$chart_type,         color = "#E69F00",         label = "data",         data = filtered_data(),         mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")       ) |>       setAxisFormat(xLabel = "Weight (1000 lbs)", yLabel = "Miles per Gallon") |>       setMargin(top = 20, bottom = 70, left = 60, right = 10)   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Shiny Integration
text: setBrush() enables rectangle selection chart. selected data points available Shiny reactive input: brush input key follows pattern myIO-{outputId}-brushed. payload includes: data — array selected row objects keys — _source_key values selected point extent — brush bounds data coordinates Use direction = "x" direction = "y" single-axis brushing.
code: library(shiny) library(myIO)  ui <- fluidPage(   titlePanel("Brush Selection"),   fluidRow(     column(8, myIOOutput("chart", height = "400px")),     column(4,       h4("Selected Points"),       verbatimTextOutput("selected")     )   ) )  server <- function(input, output) {   output$chart <- renderMyIO({     myIO() |>       addIoLayer(         type = "point",         color = "#4E79A7",         label = "scatter",         data = mtcars,         mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")       ) |>       setBrush() |>       setAxisFormat(xLabel = "Weight", yLabel = "MPG")   })    output$selected <- renderPrint({     brushed <- input$`myIO-chart-brushed`     if (is.null(brushed)) return("Drag to select points")     sel <- jsonlite::fromJSON(brushed)     if (length(sel$keys) == 0) return("No points selected")     paste(length(sel$keys), "points selected")   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Shiny Integration
text: setAnnotation() enables click--label mode. annotation stored structured data available Shiny reactive: annotation input key myIO-{outputId}-annotated. annotation includes _source_key, x, y, label, category (color), timestamp.
code: library(shiny) library(myIO)  ui <- fluidPage(   titlePanel("Data Annotation"),   fluidRow(     column(8, myIOOutput("chart", height = "400px")),     column(4,       h4("Annotations"),       tableOutput("annotations")     )   ) )  server <- function(input, output) {   output$chart <- renderMyIO({     myIO() |>       addIoLayer(         type = "point",         color = "#4E79A7",         label = "scatter",         data = mtcars,         mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")       ) |>       setAnnotation(         labels = c("outlier", "interesting", "normal"),         colors = c(outlier = "#E63946", interesting = "#F4A261", normal = "#2A9D8F")       ) |>       setAxisFormat(xLabel = "Weight", yLabel = "MPG")   })    output$annotations <- renderTable({     ann <- input$`myIO-chart-annotated`     if (is.null(ann)) return(data.frame())     parsed <- jsonlite::fromJSON(ann)     if (length(parsed$annotations) == 0) return(data.frame())     parsed$annotations[, c("label", "x", "y", "category")]   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Shiny Integration
text: setLinked() connects two myIO charts via Crosstalk. Brushing points one chart highlights : charts share SharedData object. mode parameter controls direction: "source" emits selections, "target" receives , "" (default) . Set filter = TRUE hide non-matching points instead dimming .
code: library(shiny) library(myIO) library(crosstalk)  ui <- fluidPage(   titlePanel("Linked Brushing"),   fluidRow(     column(6, myIOOutput("scatter1", height = "350px")),     column(6, myIOOutput("scatter2", height = "350px"))   ) )  server <- function(input, output) {   shared <- crosstalk::SharedData$new(mtcars, key = ~rownames(mtcars))    output$scatter1 <- renderMyIO({     myIO() |>       addIoLayer(         type = "point",         color = "#4E79A7",         label = "wt vs mpg",         data = shared$data(),         mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")       ) |>       setBrush() |>       setLinked(shared, mode = "source") |>       setAxisFormat(xLabel = "Weight", yLabel = "MPG")   })    output$scatter2 <- renderMyIO({     myIO() |>       addIoLayer(         type = "point",         color = "#E15759",         label = "hp vs mpg",         data = shared$data(),         mapping = list(x_var = "hp", y_var = "mpg")       ) |>       setLinked(shared, mode = "target") |>       setAxisFormat(xLabel = "Horsepower", yLabel = "MPG")   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Shiny Integration
text: setSlider() adds slider chart sends value Shiny input. useful adjusting transform parameters (confidence level, smoothing span, polynomial degree) without building separate sidebar: slider input key myIO-{outputId}-slider-{param}. Use debounce control often slider fires (default 200ms).
code: library(shiny) library(myIO)  ui <- fluidPage(   titlePanel("Interactive Regression"),   myIOOutput("chart", height = "450px") )  server <- function(input, output) {   output$chart <- renderMyIO({     ci <- input$`myIO-chart-slider-ci_level` %||% 0.95      myIO(data = mtcars) |>       addIoLayer(         type = "regression",         label = "fit",         mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg"),         options = list(method = "lm", showCI = TRUE, level = ci)       ) |>       setSlider("ci_level", "Confidence Level", 0.80, 0.99, ci, 0.01) |>       setAxisFormat(xLabel = "Weight", yLabel = "MPG")   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Shiny Integration
text: Add multiple myIOOutput() calls display several charts side side. chart gets output ID:
code: library(shiny) library(myIO)  ui <- fluidPage(   titlePanel("Multiple Charts"),   fluidRow(     column(6, myIOOutput("scatter", height = "350px")),     column(6, myIOOutput("bars", height = "350px"))   ) )  server <- function(input, output) {   output$scatter <- renderMyIO({     myIO() |>       addIoLayer(         type = "point",         color = "#56B4E9",         label = "scatter",         data = mtcars,         mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")       ) |>       setAxisFormat(xLabel = "Weight", yLabel = "MPG")   })    output$bars <- renderMyIO({     myIO() |>       addIoLayer(         type = "bar",         color = "#E69F00",         label = "bars",         data = mtcars,         mapping = list(x_var = "cyl", y_var = "mpg")       ) |>       defineCategoricalAxis(xAxis = TRUE) |>       setAxisFormat(xLabel = "Cylinders", yLabel = "MPG")   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: addIoLayer(): Unknown layer type 'scatter'. mean 'point'? used type name doesn’t exist. myIO suggests closest match. Use one 20 supported types listed ?addIoLayer.
code: # Wrong addIoLayer(type = "scatter", ...)  # Right addIoLayer(type = "point", ...)

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: addIoLayer(): Column 'weight' found data. Available columns: mpg, cyl, disp, hp, ... column name mapping doesn’t match column data. Check spelling case — R column names case-sensitive.
code: # Wrong — 'weight' doesn't exist in mtcars addIoLayer(mapping = list(x_var = "weight", y_var = "mpg"), ...)  # Right — the column is 'wt' addIoLayer(mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg"), ...)  # Check your column names first names(mtcars)

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: addIoLayer(): Transform 'lm' valid layer type 'bar'. transforms work chart types. example, lm works line (produces fitted values trend line).
code: # Wrong — can't apply regression to a bar chart addIoLayer(type = "bar", transform = "lm", ...)  # Right — use 'line' for trend lines addIoLayer(type = "line", transform = "lm", ...)

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: addIoLayer(): Layer label 'data' already exists. layer must unique label. Every layer needs unique label. ’re adding multiple layers, give one distinct name.
code: # Wrong — same label used twice myIO() |>   addIoLayer(type = "point", label = "data", ...) |>   addIoLayer(type = "line", label = "data", ...)  # Right — unique labels myIO() |>   addIoLayer(type = "point", label = "scatter", ...) |>   addIoLayer(type = "line", label = "trend", ...)

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: setSlider(): \param` must single character string, numeric (123).` function tells exactly expected gave . Check argument types ?setSlider.
code: # Wrong — param should be a string, not a number setSlider(123, "label", 0, 1, 0.5)  # Right setSlider("ci_level", "Confidence Level", 0.80, 0.99, 0.95)

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: setLinked(): \shared_data` must SharedData object, data.frame.` setLinked() requires crosstalk::SharedData object, raw data frame. Wrap data first.
code: library(crosstalk)  # Wrong — passing raw data.frame myIO() |> setLinked(mtcars)  # Right — wrap in SharedData shared <- SharedData$new(mtcars, key = ~rownames(mtcars)) myIO() |>   addIoLayer(type = "point", label = "pts",     data = shared$data(), mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")) |>   setLinked(shared)

title: Troubleshooting
text: Error: Expected myIO widget, got 'list'. passed something myIO() widget setter function. Make sure first argument pipe myIO().
code: # Wrong — list is not a myIO widget setBrush(list())  # Right — start with myIO() myIO() |>   addIoLayer(type = "point", label = "pts",     data = mtcars, mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")) |>   setBrush()

title: Why myIO
text: R excellent interactive visualization packages. build another one? myIO addresses specific gap ecosystem: Translation layers lose statistical annotations. Converting ggplot2 objects interactive formats can drop confidence interval ribbons, regression equations, label geoms. inherent limitation translating grammars. Statistical overlays require manual assembly. interactive packages, users must pre-compute confidence intervals, regression diagnostics, error bars R, manually layer onto charts. tedious error-prone. Native R-side computation enables composability. computing transforms R rendering D3.js, myIO avoids translation artifacts entirely. statistical layer rendering layer connect clean data contract. myIO solves composable transform pipeline: statistical computation happens R (belongs), rendering happens D3.js (’s beautiful), two connect clean data contract.

title: Why myIO
text: Confidence interval bands notoriously difficult render correctly interactive charts built translation layers. myIO computes CI bands natively R renders first-class area layer: ci transform uses stats::predict() interval = "confidence" outputs grid low_y / high_y bounds. area renderer displays smooth band. Prediction intervals work way options = list(interval = "prediction").
code: myIO(data = mtcars) |>   addIoLayer(type = "point", color = "#4E79A7", label = "Data",     mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")) |>   addIoLayer(type = "line", color = "#E15759", label = "Trend",     transform = "lm",     mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")) |>   addIoLayer(type = "area", color = "#E15759", label = "95% CI",     transform = "ci",     mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg"),     options = list(level = 0.95))

title: Why myIO
text: Displaying regression equation alongside interactive chart typically requires multiple packages manual assembly. myIO’s regression composite handles entire workflow one call: auto-expands four sub-layers: scatter points, trend line, CI band, R² annotation — styled consistently. Change method "loess" "polynomial" switch model.
code: myIO(data = mtcars) |>   addIoLayer(type = "regression", label = "MPG vs Weight",     mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg"),     options = list(method = "lm", showCI = TRUE, showStats = TRUE))

title: Why myIO
text: Every myIO chart uses pattern: type + transform = layer. Transforms R functions compute statistical summaries return data frame. renderer doesn’t know care numbers mean — just plots fields. means can compose transforms freely: Available transforms: transforms use base R’s stats package — additional dependencies.
code: # Scatter + LOESS smooth + CI band + residual plot myIO(data = mtcars) |>   addIoLayer(type = "point", label = "Data",     mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg")) |>   addIoLayer(type = "line", label = "LOESS", transform = "loess",     mapping = list(x_var = "wt", y_var = "mpg"),     options = list(span = 0.5))

title: Why myIO
text: Complex statistical charts like boxplots violins defined composites auto-expand simpler layers: sub-layer renders independently, means: IQR box can different color whiskers Outliers can toggled /via options = list(showOutliers = TRUE) Tooltips work every sub-component Animations layered (whiskers grow box edges, caps appear) don’t need know decomposition — just call addIoLayer(type = "boxplot", ...) works. need custom control, can compose sub-layers manually.
code: boxplot → rangeBar (IQR) + point (whisker caps) + point (median) + point (outliers) violin  → area (density) + rangeBar (IQR box) + point (median) regression → point (scatter) + line (trend) + area (CI band) + text (R²)

title: Why myIO
text: Mean ± confidence interval bars standard scientific publications. interactive viz packages, must compute CI manually assemble layers. myIO one call: mean_ci transform computes group mean, standard error, t-distribution CI bounds — matching stats::t.test() output exactly.
code: myIO(data = iris) |>   addIoLayer(type = "rangeBar", label = "Mean ± 95% CI",     transform = "mean_ci",     mapping = list(x_var = "Species", y_var = "Sepal.Length"),     options = list(level = 0.95)) |>   defineCategoricalAxis(xAxis = TRUE) |>   setAxisFormat(xLabel = "Species", yLabel = "Sepal Length")

title: Why myIO
text: myIO follows three principles: R computes, D3 renders. Statistical computation stays R ecosystem strongest. JavaScript handles rendering interaction. translation layer can break. Type + transform = layer. Every chart built two concepts. makes API small predictable — 15 transforms 18 chart types compose hundreds visualizations. Composites expand primitives. Complex charts decompose simpler ones. means new statistical overlays don’t require new renderers — reuse existing ones.

what: myIO: Interactive Data Visualizations Using d3.js — myIO-package
title: myIO: Interactive Data Visualizations Using d3.js — myIO-package
text: Create interactive 'd3.js' visualizations R built-statistical transforms. Computes confidence intervals, regression fits, LOESS smoothing, moving averages, error bars, uncertainty visualizations (quantile dot plots fan charts) R renders composable chart layers via 'htmlwidgets'. Supports 36 chart types including boxplots, violin plots, Q-Q diagnostic plots, calendar heatmaps, survival curves, group comparisons pairwise significance testing. Also provides machine-readable chart specification schema validators large language model agents can author verify charts. Works 'RStudio', 'Shiny', 'R Markdown'.

title: Create a myIO Chart Widget — myIO
text: data optional point entry data frame vector width string either pixel width percentage width height string pixel height elementId unique id htmlwidget object title Optional chart title rendered inside widget SVG. sparkline Logical. TRUE, renders compact sparkline suitable embedding table cells. Strips axes, legend, interactions, floating action button. "line", "bar", "area" layer types supported. Default FALSE. engine one "auto" (default), "server", "wasm", "svg". consulted big-data features attached via setBigData(). big-data attachment, charts render identically small-data SVG path regardless argument. See vignette("large-data-linking"). webgl_threshold Positive integer row-count threshold big-data WebGL render path. Use Inf disable WebGL. unify_data_path = TRUE, disabled WebGL uses SVG coordinator path; otherwise existing inline SVG path preserved. Default 50000. unify_data_path Logical. TRUE, coordinator results also replace SVG layer data webgl_threshold. Default FALSE preserves inline small-data SVG render path.

title: Update a myIO chart in place from the Shiny server — myIOProxy
text: `myIOProxy()` creates lightweight handle already-rendered myIO widget, `updateMyIOData()` swaps data one existing layers without re-rendering whole widget. Unlike re-executing `renderMyIO()` (destroys recreates chart every reactive invalidation, dropping brush/zoom/toggle state flickering), proxy update reuses existing data-join path: changed marks transition, interaction state preserved.

text: Splits chart grid panels, one per unique value faceting variable. panel shows layers filtered subset data.

code: setFacet(   myIO,   var,   ncol = NULL,   minWidth = NULL,   scales = "fixed",   labelPosition = NULL,   ... )

title: Set Faceting (Small Multiples) — setFacet
text: myIO myIO widget object. var Character. Column name facet . Must exist least one layer's data. ncol Integer NULL. Number columns grid. NULL, auto-computes minWidth container width. minWidth Numeric. Minimum panel width pixels ncol NULL. Default 200. scales Character. Scale sharing mode: "fixed" – panels share x y scales (default) "free_x" – independent x scales per panel "free_y" – independent y scales per panel "free" – independent x y scales per panel labelPosition Character. show panel labels: "top" (default) "bottom". ... reserved; accepts deprecated min_width label_position aliases minWidth labelPosition.

title: Enable Linked Brushing via Crosstalk — setLinked
text: myIO htmlwidget object created myIO() function shared_data crosstalk::SharedData object mode "source", "target", "" (default) filter TRUE, Crosstalk filter operations hide non-matching points. Default FALSE (dim ). key Optional character vector row keys. supplied, overrides keys extracted shared_data. Useful SharedData keys match column used cross-chart matching. group Optional character string. supplied, overrides Crosstalk group name shared_data, allowing manual control widgets share selections. cursor Logical. TRUE, hover linked chart draws synchronized crosshair every sibling chart group. Default FALSE. cursorAxis Character. axis sync: "x" (default), "y", "xy". "x" active v1.2.

New setTransition(duration, easing, stagger) configures chart animations: duration milliseconds, easing (one "linear", "quad", "cubic", "sin", "exp", "circle", "back", "bounce", "elastic", mapped corresponding d3 easing), stagger (per-element cascade delay ms). arguments optional additive; unset values keep renderer’s existing defaults, change fully backward compatible. setTransitionSpeed() now thin wrapper setTransition(duration = ). Animation stays fully opt--able: duration = 0 disables , easing stagger automatically -op effective duration 0, including viewer’s prefers-reduced-motion: reduce system setting. Playwright e2e spec verifies animate--, still--, still--reduced-motion. New opt-"lttb" transform line layers downsamples large series Largest-Triangle-Three-Buckets, shipping options$threshold points (default 2000) preserving visual shape: addIoLayer(type = "line", transform = "lttb", options = list(threshold = 1000)). default (identity); runs -memory/SVG path independent DuckDB-WASM engine’s SQL-side LTTB, never double-downsamples. New myIOProxy() + updateMyIOData() update rendered chart’s layer data place Shiny server without re-running renderMyIO(). Layers matched label swapped existing data-join path, changed marks transition brush/zoom/toggle state preserved (full re-render destroyed recreated chart, flickering dropping state): myIOProxy("chart") |> updateMyIOData(series = new_df). setLegendTitle() puts title legend naming variable entries come , grouped chart whose series labeled 5 6 7 8 9 can say months. title renders whichever legend surface active – compact -plot strip panel behind legend button – exported SVG, PNG PDF. title: myIO 1.3.0
text: Argument names now consistently camelCase across setters. setBrush(onSelect), setFacet(minWidth, labelPosition), setTheme(textColor, gridColor), setBigData(rowkeyCol) canonical forms (matching colorScheme, xAxis, etc.). previous snake_case names (on_select, min_width, label_position, text_color, grid_color, rowkey_col) keep working deprecated aliases emit one-line warning; existing code unaffected aside warning. forms supplied camelCase value wins. setFacet(), setLayerOpacity(), setTheme(mode = ) now report invalid arguments consistent, actionable messages (e.g. setFacet(): \scales` must “fixed”, “free_x”, “free_y”, “free”, “x”.) instead barestopifnot()failures.setColorScheme()` errors likewise function-prefixed. change inputs accepted. setTheme() now warns passed unknown argument lacks required -- prefix (e.g. misspelled text_colour) suggests intended argument, instead silently dropping . Valid ---prefixed CSS overrides unaffected. setTheme() documents named preset values ("midnight", "ocean", "forest", "sunset", "monochrome", "neon", "corporate", "academic", "nature", "minimal", "retro", "warm", plus "light"/"dark"); preset argument already functional. setLinked() linkCharts() now cross-reference documentation clarify use Crosstalk path versus group-identifier path.

title: myIO 1.3.0

title: myIO 1.3.0
text: Inline Arrow IPC payloads now decode via native Uint8Array.fromBase64 browser provides (falling back previous atob loop), avoiding per-character JavaScript callback large payloads -memory DuckDB-WASM engines. Added regression test confirming charts already render inline legend given duplicated legend image/SVG export (GH #64). Layer-data serialization (addIoLayer()) faster large data: row-rectangling step now extracts columns indexes per row instead subsetting data frame every row, roughly 5x faster 100k rows. emitted JSON byte-identical (pinned tests across numeric, integer, character, logical, factor, Date, POSIXct columns), every chart type renders exactly .

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-06-11

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: New machine-readable chart specification schema (inst/myio-schema.json) describing chart types, required mappings, valid transforms, function signatures, generated package’s contracts. Six exported R tools let large language model agents author verify charts schema: myio_list_chart_types(), myio_chart_schema(), myio_validate_spec(), myio_list_functions(), myio_function_signature(), myio_validate_call(). Model Context Protocol server package’s source repository exposes six tools MCP-compatible clients. New vignette llm-tool-calling demonstrates generate-validate-repair loop.

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: New quantile_dots chart type quantile_dots transform render Wilkinson dot plot predictive quantiles communicating uncertainty. New fan composite renders fan chart nested prediction intervals around central estimate.

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: myIO(title = ...) setTitle() add backward-compatible chart title surface rendered inside SVG. Existing charts omit title unchanged. Axis titles setAxisFormat(xLabel = ..., yLabel = ...) now render chart SVG, multi-series charts get compact visible legend preserving existing action-sheet legend. gallery now carries chart titles across examples, repairs horizontal bars, mean-CI, heatmap margins, gauge thresholds, treemap labels, date-based finance examples, shows themes across small grid representative charts.

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: setLinked() now links waffle, beeswarm, lollipop, dumbbell layers addition previously supported point, bar, groupedBar, histogram, hexbin. Selection dims non-matching elements; filter hides . Aggregate chart types (boxplot, violin, qq, regression, density, ridgeline, survfit, comparison) remain outside crosstalk v1.2. New vignette crosstalk-linking demonstrates linking myIO DT::datatable() reactable::reactable(), code listings plotly leaflet.

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: myIO() widgets now declare sizing policy browser.fill = TRUE tagged html-fill-item via htmltools::bindFillRole(), fill container height inside bslib::card(), Quarto Dashboard {.fill} cards, flexdashboard layouts. Rendering plain RMarkdown Shiny default 400px height unchanged. Widget resize now guarded zero-dimension containers can appear briefly fill-layout transitions.

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: New calendarHeatmap chart type — GitHub-contributions-style grid daily cells single calendar year. Usage: addIoLayer(type = "calendarHeatmap", data, mapping = list(date = "day", value = "x")). Supports Sunday Monday week starts via options$weekStart, continuous color legend, linked-cursor sync across two linked calendars. Multi-year data rejected v1.2; multi-year layouts planned v1.3. New CSS variables: --chart-calendar-cell-gap, --chart-calendar-cell-stroke, --chart-calendar-empty-fill.

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: 12 named theme presets: setTheme(preset = "midnight"). Available presets: midnight, ocean, forest, sunset, monochrome, neon, corporate, academic, nature, minimal, retro, warm. Plus light/dark via mode parameter.

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: linkCharts(chart1, chart2, = "column") enables cross-chart selection. Brush one chart highlights matching rows linked charts. Works Shiny static HTML. Aggregation--source-row key resolution summary views.

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: linkCharts() setLinked() gain cursor = TRUE argument draws synchronized vertical crosshair every linked chart user hovers chart group. Supports point, bar, line, area, groupedBar, hexbin, histogram layers (donut treemap excluded — x-axis sync ). default; enable per-link retrofit setLinkedCursor() pre-linked widget. New --chart-cursor-rule-color/-width/-dasharray CSS variables theme crosshair.

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: Pass dplyr::group_by() tibble addIoLayer() auto-creates one layer per group colors Okabe-Ito palette. Soft dplyr dependency.

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: addIoLayer(type = "survfit", mapping = list(time = "time", status = "status")) computes Kaplan-Meier estimator Greenwood CI using base R (survival package dependency). Composite expands step-curve line, CI band, censored-observation markers. Group stratification supported.

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: addIoLayer(type = "histogram_fit", mapping = list(value = "x"), options = list(family = "normal")) fits normal, lognormal, exponential distributions via MLE. Composite renders histogram + fitted density curve + optional parameter annotation.

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: setLayerOpacity(label, opacity) sets per-layer opacity (0-1). Critical CI bands overlaying scatter data.

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: ARIA roles (graphics-document, graphics-object, graphics-symbol) applied SVG chart structure screen reader navigation. text: lollipop — vertical stem circle head, supports mean summary transforms. Standalone. beeswarm — dodge-positioned points avoid overlap. title: myIO 1.2.0
text: setFacet(var, ncol, scales) splits charts CSS grid panels, one per unique value faceting variable. Supports fixed free scale modes, auto-layout configurable minimum panel width, responsive breakpoints.

title: myIO 1.2.0
text: setTheme(mode = "dark") applies WCAG AA-verified dark palette across chart elements. Also supports "light" "auto" (detects OS preference Quarto/Bootstrap data-bs-theme). title: myIO 1.2.0
text: myIO(sparkline = TRUE) renders compact, axes-free chart suitable embedding table cells (reactable, DT, gt). Strips legend, axes, reference lines, interactions. Default height 20px. Supports line, bar, area layer types.

title: myIO 1.0.0
text: New composable transform pipeline: type + transform = layer. Transforms compute statistics R; renderers display D3.js. Transforms: lm, loess, polynomial, ci, smooth, mean, mean_ci, residuals, summary, pairwise_test, qq. Composite chart expansion: complex charts decompose primitive layers.

title: myIO 1.0.0
text: Basic: line, point, bar, area, groupedBar. Statistical: histogram, hexbin, regression, qq. Distribution: boxplot, violin, ridgeline, comparison. Financial: candlestick, waterfall, heatmap. Standalone: donut, gauge, treemap, sankey.
